target.title: fix(cron): detect ===DONE_ERR=== sentinel in agent final text as failure signal
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An isolated agent cron turn whose final text explicitly declares failure via the `===DONE_ERR===` terminal sentinel is recorded as a successful run, causing `failureAlert` to never fire. The sentinel text is now recognized as a fatal failure signal in the shared cron outcome resolver.

- Problem: `resolveCronPayloadOutcome()` only checks structured signals (`payload.isError`, `runLevelError`, `failureSignal`) and ignores agent final visible text that contains a `===DONE_ERR===` failure sentinel, so the run is recorded as `ok` even when the agent self-reported failure.
- Solution: Detect the `===DONE_ERR===` sentinel in the last non-empty line of `finalAssistantVisibleText` and synthesize a `CronFailureSignal` with `fatalForCron: true`, causing `hasFatalErrorPayload` to be set correctly.
- What changed: `src/cron/isolated-agent/helpers.ts` (~15 lines in `resolveCronPayloadOutcome`), `src/cron/isolated-agent/helpers.test.ts` (8 new test cases).
- What did NOT change: Function signature, exported API, structured error signal handling, delivery paths, outer cron scheduler.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #111405
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Isolated cron agent jobs that use the `===DONE_ERR===` convention to signal failure (agent's final text ending with this sentinel) are recorded as successful runs. The `lastRunStatus` stays `ok`, `consecutiveErrors` is reset, and per-job `failureAlert` never fires. This silent failure masking causes operators to miss persistent cron failures.

The existing `resolveCronPayloadOutcome` function already has the `finalAssistantVisibleText` parameter available — it was only used for delivery text selection, never for failure classification. Adding sentinel detection leverages the existing data path with no new parameters or wiring.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: `===DONE_ERR===` sentinel in agent final text now correctly sets `hasFatalErrorPayload=true` and populates `embeddedRunError`
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 22.22.3, `fix/cron-done-err-sentinel-111405`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/isolated-agent/helpers.test.ts --run
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/isolated-agent/ --run
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/isolated-agent/helpers.test.ts --run
 RUN  v4.1.10

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  20 passed (20)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/isolated-agent/ --run
 Test Files  34 passed (34)
      Tests  480 passed (480)
```

**Matrix-style evidence**:

| Input variant | `hasFatalErrorPayload` | `embeddedRunError` |
|---|---|---|
| `finalAssistantVisibleText: "===DONE_ERR=== vault delivery blocked"` | `true` | Contains sentinel |
| `finalAssistantVisibleText: "multi-line\n===DONE_ERR=== err"` | `true` | Contains sentinel |
| `finalAssistantVisibleText: "===DONE_ERR=== mid\nrecovered\nok"` | `false` | `undefined` |
| `finalAssistantVisibleText: "===DONE_OK=== vault updated"` | `false` | `undefined` |
| `finalAssistantVisibleText: "Normal output"` | `false` | `undefined` |
| No `finalAssistantVisibleText` | `false` | `undefined` |
| `failureSignal: {fatalForCron: true}` + sentinel | `true` | Uses explicit signal |
| Structured `isError` payload + sentinel | `true` | Uses structured error |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. Agent text ending with `===DONE_ERR=== <reason>` → `hasFatalErrorPayload=true`, `embeddedRunError` contains the sentinel
  2. Multi-line text with sentinel on last line → correctly detected
  3. `===DONE_ERR===` in middle of text (not last line) → **not** detected (by design — agent recovered)
  4. `===DONE_OK===` → no effect (already success without sentinel)
  5. Explicit fatal `failureSignal` takes priority over sentinel detection
  6. Structured error payloads independently cause `hasFatalErrorPayload=true`
- What was not tested: Real gateway end-to-end with a cron agentTurn job (requires full cron + agent setup with a model provider)
- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**:
  - ✅ Auth guard: Not needed — sentinel detection has no auth implications
  - ✅ Enum completeness: Covers `===DONE_ERR===`, non-matching text, explicit failureSignal priority
  - ✅ Path coverage: Shared resolver covers both finalization and interim ack detection paths
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: Synthetic signal flows through existing normalization path

## Root Cause

`resolveCronPayloadOutcome()` (in `src/cron/isolated-agent/helpers.ts`) only classifies runs as fatal based on structured signals (`payload.isError`, `runLevelError`, `failureSignal`). The `finalAssistantVisibleText` parameter was only used for delivery text selection, not for content-based failure detection. When an agent ends its final text with `===DONE_ERR===` — a conventional sentinel used by agent systems — the run was recorded as successful.

Introduced by commit `060b30f23a1` (2026-07-18).

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Cron jobs using `===DONE_ERR===` sentinel in agent final text will now be recorded as failed, triggering `consecutiveErrors` tracking and `failureAlert`. Previously these runs were silently recorded as successful.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: All 8 input variants in the evidence matrix; all 480 isolated-agent cron tests pass
- Edge cases checked: Multi-line text, sentinel in middle, explicit failureSignal priority, no text, structured error payloads
- What you did NOT verify: Real gateway end-to-end with a model provider

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only new behavior is detecting `===DONE_ERR===`; existing runs without this sentinel are unaffected
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — the shared `resolveCronPayloadOutcome` is the correct boundary because it already consumes `finalAssistantVisibleText` and all cron isolated-agent outcome paths route through it.
- **Refactor needed**: No — single-function change, no architecture or API changes.
- **Alternative considered**: Adding a configurable pattern for failure sentinels — rejected as over-engineering for one well-established convention; can be extended later if more patterns emerge.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Agents that include `===DONE_ERR===` in final text for informational purposes (not as a failure signal) would see their runs classified as failed.

**Mitigation**: The detection only triggers on the **last non-empty line** of the agent's final visible text — `===DONE_ERR===` in the middle of text, followed by recovery, is correctly ignored. The sentinel must be an exact `===DONE_ERR===` prefix match. Explicit `failureSignal` takes priority.

**Compatibility impact**: None for existing jobs that do not use this sentinel.

---

Fixes #111405
